risks.note: FY2025-26 US tariff actions (raising the effective rate on Indian textile exports to 50% before easing to 18% under an interim agreement) disrupted order flows, sourcing calendars and export visibility across the industry for nearly two quarters; the Company's own EBITDA margin declined 56 bps to 6.48% amid the disruption.

The Company's export revenues have historically been concentrated in specific markets (South Korea and, increasingly, Bangladesh); the AR itself frames this as a structural vulnerability at the industry level (US+EU together were ~49% of India's textile exports pre-diversification) that the Company has been actively working to diversify away from.

EBITDA margin moderated from 7.04% to 6.48% and PAT margin moderated from 2.49% to 2.39% in FY2025-26, attributed to higher input costs, a change in revenue mix and higher financing costs, indicating margins are sensitive to these factors even amid revenue growth.
risks.risk: Margin sensitivity to input and financing costs

risks.note: RoCE declined from 51.52% (FY24) to 29.66% (FY25) to 22.66% (FY26), which the Company attributes to the capital base expanding (post-IPO) ahead of full deployment into productive assets; realisation of the expected medium-term RoCE recovery depends on successful deployment and commissioning of new assets.

The receivables cycle lengthened to 96 days from 85 days in the previous year, reflecting trade credit extended to domestic customers to support domestic sales growth, increasing working-capital and collection risk even though export receivables are largely covered by letters of credit and a domestic trade-credit insurance policy.

The Company's strategic extension into in-house sizing, warping and processing capability is still at the project-report stage ('under finalisation'); investment outlay, implementation schedule and expected benefits had not yet been communicated at the time of reporting.
risks.risk: Execution risk on new processing/value-addition initiative

- The Company's export revenues have historically been concentrated in specific markets (South Korea and, increasingly, Bangladesh); the AR itself frames this as a structural vulnerability at the industry level (US+EU together were ~49% of India's textile exports pre-diversification) that the Company has been actively working to diversify away from.
- EBITDA margin moderated from 7.04% to 6.48% and PAT margin moderated from 2.49% to 2.39% in FY2025-26, attributed to higher input costs, a change in revenue mix and higher financing costs, indicating margins are sensitive to these factors even amid revenue growth.
- RoCE declined from 51.52% (FY24) to 29.66% (FY25) to 22.66% (FY26), which the Company attributes to the capital base expanding (post-IPO) ahead of full deployment into productive assets; realisation of the expected medium-term RoCE recovery depends on successful deployment and commissioning of new assets.
- The receivables cycle lengthened to 96 days from 85 days in the previous year, reflecting trade credit extended to domestic customers to support domestic sales growth, increasing working-capital and collection risk even though export receivables are largely covered by letters of credit and a domestic trade-credit insurance policy.
- The Company's strategic extension into in-house sizing, warping and processing capability is still at the project-report stage ('under finalisation'); investment outlay, implementation schedule and expected benefits had not yet been communicated at the time of reporting.
